title: Nova Health - POC scoping / commercial guardrails
summary: Quick POC-scoping call to align on success criteria, workload sizing and commercial guardrails for an 8-week pilot. Key asks: p95 latency <300ms for single-turn summaries, throughput target 20 qps sustained, accuracy/regression thresholds defined vs current in-house model. Discussed trial credits, pilot terms (8 weeks), and procurement path (SOW -> PO -> committed reserved capacity). Redwood to run benchmarks and provide cost model + security docs.
topics: Benchmark plan and metrics (p50/p95 latency, tokens/sec, cost)
Commercial guardrails (credits, trial length, conversion discounts)
Procurement path and required docs (SOC2, ISO, SSO, KMS)
action_items: Alex Martinez (Redwood AE): Send POC commercial proposal and pilot credit breakdown by 2025-08-14
Priya Desai (Redwood SE): Schedule benchmark run and confirm target test dataset; provide benchmark plan by 2025-08-15
Tom Reed (Nova Health): Share representative dataset samples and performance success criteria doc by 2025-08-14
Mark Powell (Nova Health Procurement): Share procurement timeline and PO template by 2025-08-18
next_steps: Redwood to run initial benchmarks on 3 candidate model variants (open quantized, 8-bit, full FP16) using Nova sample dataset
Redwood to propose trial credits (equivalent to $15k list usage) for 8-week pilot; convert to committed reserved capacity pricing if conversion within 90 days
Schedule technical deep-dive (SE-led) to review network topology for VPC options and KMS integration
Procurement: exchange contracting contacts and required security/insurance docs
transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-08-12 15:00 PDT | Duration: 54 minutes | Attendees: Alex (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Tom (Head of ML - Nova Health), Sarah (CTO), Mark (Procurement), Jenna (Data Eng)

[00:00] Alex: hey everyone, thanks for joining, i'm alex with redwood inference, i'll kick us off. really quick agenda: scope the poc, agree success criteria, sizing, and talk commercial guardrails. priya will jump in on benchmarks.
[00:18] Tom: hi alex, thanks. we're looking to replace our in-house summarization pipeline, primarily to reduce latency and cost. target is roughly 2k tokens per request for long summaries, but most are in the 300-800 token range.
[00:35] Sarah: and security is a must, SOC2 and SSO, also we need audit logs for any PHI exposure, right now we can't send raw PHI off-prem without controls.
[00:48] Alex: totally — we support VPC/private deploy options, KMS integration for key separation, and audit logs; we'll share the security pack after this call.
[01:05] Priya: quick question on expected qps and concurrency — Tom, what steady-state traffic do you expect for the pilot?
[01:12] Tom: for the pilot, around 20 qps sustained, spikes to 80 qps with short bursts. concurrency per worker probably ~10-20. it's mostly single-turn calls but some multi-turn conversational traces exist.
[01:26] Priya: ok that's helpful; for throughput planning we'll pick model variants that can meet p95 latency under 300ms for the 300-800 token requests and under 600ms for the 2k token tail. we'll run end-to-end tests including network egress.
[01:45] Sarah: cost is also a tradeoff — if latency is great but cost doubles, we'll have pushback. what's the typical pilot credit structure?
[01:54] Alex: we usually offer pilot credits to cover baseline usage — for this size we'd propose credits equivalent to ~$15k list usage, with an 8-week pilot term. conversion discounts depend on commit size; we'll outline those in the POC proposal.
[02:10] Mark: procurement will want firm term sheets: pilot credits, what gets billed post-pilot, what converts to reserved capacity, and a path to a statement of work. Also need vendor security docs up front.
[02:23] Alex: understood. we'll include a procurement packet: SOC2, ISO attestation, SSO/SAML docs, sample SLA, and a standard SOW template.
[02:35] Jenna: about the dataset — i can share a representative sample, but there's PHI redaction; is it ok if we obfuscate fields?
[02:43] Priya: yes obfuscated samples are fine for latency/throughput benchmarks; for model quality/regression tests we'll need either synthetic or privacy-preserving subsets — we can accept hashed IDs.
[03:00] Tom: success criteria: p95 latency <300ms for short summaries, p95 <600ms for 2k token edge cases, cost per 1k tokens less than our current infra by at least 20%, and zero functional regressions on our evaluation prompts (we'll provide eval set).
[03:20] Priya: we'll run baseline against your eval set and produce a quality matrix — accuracy and hallucination metrics — and flag regressions. we normally set a soft regression threshold of <=2% on critical prompts.
[03:36] Alex: commercial guardrails: pilot credits are one-time, cover hosted API usage. If you want dedicated reserved capacity for the pilot (to guarantee throughput), we can offer a short-term reserved pool with limited commit and a pilot discount — depends on expected utilization.
[03:55] Sarah: for regulatory reasons, we might need private deployment in a VPC — is there a separate charge or longer lead time?
[04:03] Alex: private deployments have onboarding overhead. for VPC-hosted private control plane we can do it within 2-3 weeks given approvals; on-prem is longer. there may be a setup fee; we'll spell that out in the commercial proposal.
[04:20] Mark: what about data retention and egress — we need contract language that ensures logs and payloads are not stored beyond the pilot unless explicitly allowed.
[04:29] Alex: yes, we'll include retention clauses and a data handling appendix; default behavior will be no retention of request payloads unless you enable logging for debugging.
[04:40] Priya: on benchmarks — plan is: 1) perf microbench to select model variant; 2) end-to-end latency with your sample dataset across 3 regions; 3) sustained throughput with concurrency profiles; 4) cost extrapolation. we'll provide scripts and host a dashboard.
[05:02] Tom: timeline? we need results before our leadership review at the end of september.
[05:08] Priya: we can run the initial benchmark within 7 business days after we receive samples and network access details; fully staged pilot ~8 weeks from kick-off.
[05:16] Alex: so rough timeline: share samples + procurement contacts this week; redwood sends POC proposal + security pack by thursday; benchmark run next week; kickoff pilot the following week.
[05:29] Tom: fine. on conversion economics, what happens if we exceed credits early? do we get prorated discounts or extend pilot?
[05:37] Alex: typically overage is billed at list unless we agree otherwise; we can include an overage protection cap or optional top-up credit in the pilot agreement. conversion to committed capacity within 90 days can have retroactive credit applied depending on negotiation. we'll put options in the proposal.
[05:52] Mark: procurement will also ask about indemnity, insurance limits, and export controls — we'll send the checklist.
[05:58] Alex: we'll have legal review those items and include a redwood point of contact.
[06:05] Jenna: for the quality eval, do you run your own eval harness or do we need to run locally?
[06:11] Priya: we can run both — we run hosted evals for reproducibility and share results; if you prefer running locally in your VPC we can provide the containers and scripts.
[06:22] Tom: ok, that's great. anything else?
[06:25] Alex: quick recap of next steps: redwood to send proposal + security pack, priya to schedule benchmarks, tom to share samples and success criteria doc, mark to share procurement timeline.
[06:35] Sarah: sounds good, thanks everyone.
[06:38] Alex: thanks all — we'll follow up on the action items.

Notes: transcription contains minor mis-hearings (some acronyms garbled), occasional crosstalk.

Attachments referenced: POC proposal (to be shared), Security pack link (SOC2/ISO), Benchmark dashboard link (to be created)
notes: Pilot term: 8 weeks; Pilot credits proposed: $15k equivalent (to cover hosted API usage for test traffic); Overages billed at list unless top-up agreed; Conversion discounts negotiable depending on committed reserved capacity. Private/VPC onboarding 2-3 weeks. Success criteria doc to be supplied by customer.
